details:
=== CONSENSUS FINDINGS ===
- docs/plans/ai-code-review-learnings-plan.md:Lines 72-76 (Current state, Reviewer pass) and Phase B `full` tier model list (lines ~360-368), and Phase G failback chains (lines ~476-486) | severity=high | confidence=5
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro]
  PROBLEM: The plan's reviewer model set omits `z-ai/glm-5`, so the `full` tier and failback chain would drop a currently-active reviewer.
  WHY: The workflow and model catalog already include six reviewer models, but the plan hard-codes only five, so a literal implementation would silently exclude `z-ai/glm-5` from full reviews and failback handling.
- docs/plans/ai-code-review-learnings-plan.md:Phase B threshold definition (lines ~338-346) | severity=medium | confidence=4
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro]
  PROBLEM: `total_lines` is undefined in the `git diff --numstat`-based tiering rules, so tier assignment can vary depending on how changed lines are counted.
  WHY: `numstat` reports additions and deletions separately, but the plan does not say whether `total_lines` means additions only, additions plus deletions, or net change, which would change trivial/lite classification.
- docs/plans/ai-code-review-learnings-plan.md:Phase B trivial tier model list (lines ~360-362) | severity=medium | confidence=4
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro]
  PROBLEM: The `trivial` tier picks `openai/gpt-5.4-mini` as the only reviewer without addressing whether its output matches the review-finding contract.
  WHY: If that model does not emit the expected `=== ISSUE NNN ===` blocks, the consolidator could see zero findings and silently degrade review quality for small PRs.
- docs/plans/ai-code-review-learnings-plan.md:Phase G failback chains (lines ~476-486) | severity=medium | confidence=3
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro]
  PROBLEM: The Phase G failback chain omits `z-ai/glm-5`, leaving the sixth reviewer with no defined fallback.
  WHY: An unmapped reviewer slug would fail open, but the plan should still list the active reviewer explicitly instead of leaving the JSON incomplete.
- docs/plans/ai-code-review-learnings-plan.md:line ~140 (Cloudflare lessons row 1) | severity=low | confidence=4
  flagged_by: [qwen_qwen3_6-plus]
  PROBLEM: The claim that Cloudflare's system maps "almost 1-for-1" onto the repo's seven lenses is inaccurate.
  WHY: Cloudflare's agents are domain/role-based, while the repo's lenses are failure-mode-based, so the correspondence is only partial and the claim overstates the alignment.
- docs/plans/ai-code-review-learnings-plan.md:Phase B section | severity=medium | confidence=3
  flagged_by: [qwen_qwen3_6-plus]
  PROBLEM: The proposed Phase B tiering is underspecified relative to the existing binary reasoning gate, so the migration path is unclear.
  WHY: The plan introduces a three-tier reviewer-count system without saying how it coexists with or replaces the current 100-LOC gating variables, which risks conflicting behavior at rollout.
- docs/plans/ai-code-review-learnings-plan.md:Phase G section | severity=medium | confidence=3
  flagged_by: [qwen_qwen3_6-plus]
  PROBLEM: The Phase G failback chains assume fallback slugs exist without verifying that the slugs are resolvable.
  WHY: If a fallback slug is missing or deprecated, the retry path can fail with a model-resolution error instead of recovering from the original 429/5xx.
- docs/plans/ai-code-review-learnings-plan.md:Phase G description | severity=low | confidence=2
  flagged_by: [qwen_qwen3_6-plus]
  PROBLEM: The shared reviewer health file lacks an atomic/concurrency strategy.
  WHY: Concurrent reads and writes, or TTL handling without a clear lazy-read rule, can leave the health state stale or corrupted and suppress healthy models.
- docs/plans/ai-code-review-learnings-plan.md:Phase I description | severity=low | confidence=2
  flagged_by: [qwen_qwen3_6-plus]
  PROBLEM: The heartbeat wrapper design adds per-callsite monitoring overhead without specifying how it is implemented.
  WHY: The plan does not say whether the helper polls efficiently or busy-waits, so its actual CPU cost on GitHub Actions runners is unknown.
- docs/plans/ai-code-review-learnings-plan.md:Phase H / Constraints section | severity=medium | confidence=3
  flagged_by: [qwen_qwen3_6-plus]
  PROBLEM: `CONTEXT_BUDGET_WARN` is scoped as a stable log prefix even though the plan assigns it to an offline audit tool instead of the workflow log path.
  WHY: If only `cost_audit.py` emits it, the workflow-log-analysis pipeline will never see the prefix, so the naming contract and the consumer path do not line up.
- docs/plans/ai-code-review-learnings-plan.md:Phase H, cache_hit_rate formula (lines ~569-571) | severity=high | confidence=5
  flagged_by: [z-ai_glm-5]
  PROBLEM: The cache hit rate formula double-counts cached tokens in the denominator.
  WHY: `cache_read_input_tokens` and `cache_creation_input_tokens` are already subsets of `prompt_tokens`, so adding all three would understate the rate and report misleadingly low cache hit values.
- docs/plans/ai-code-review-learnings-plan.md:Line 79 — "The eight phases below (A–J minus K)" | severity=low | confidence=5
  flagged_by: [z-ai_glm-5]
  PROBLEM: The phase count is inconsistent: the document says "eight phases" but enumerates A through J.
  WHY: The mismatch between the narrative count and the actual phase labels can confuse implementers about scope, even though this is documentation-only.
- docs/plans/ai-code-review-learnings-plan.md:Mapping table row 13 and "Current state" section (lines ~68–70) — "Conflict-resolver failback" | severity=medium | confidence=4
  flagged_by: [z-ai_glm-5]
  PROBLEM: The plan misdescribes the conflict-resolver's existing fallback behavior as model-family failback.
  WHY: The actual script only steps reasoning effort down on the same model, so using it as the template for model-slug failback risks conflating two different resilience mechanisms.
- docs/plans/ai-code-review-learnings-plan.md:Constraints section (lines 211–212) — list of new log prefixes | severity=medium | confidence=4
  flagged_by: [z-ai_glm-5]
  PROBLEM: The Constraints section enumerates only five new stable log prefixes, while the rest of the plan adds three more.
  WHY: An incomplete normative list can cause `agents.md` documentation to miss `REVIEWER_HEALTH`, `RE_REVIEW_SKIP`, and `CONTEXT_BUDGET_WARN`.
- docs/plans/ai-code-review-learnings-plan.md:Constraints section (line ~405) — references `LINKED_ISSUE_FILE` | severity=high | confidence=4
  flagged_by: [z-ai_glm-5]
  PROBLEM: The plan refers to `LINKED_ISSUE_FILE`, but the script variable is `LINKED_ISSUE_CONTEXT_FILE`.
  WHY: Using the wrong variable name would leave the materiality reviewer with an empty or unbound path and cause it to fail open silently.
=== END CONSENSUS FINDINGS ===
